publisher_issuer: Cosi, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001171014)
company_context: Cosi was a fast-casual restaurant chain (flatbread sandwiches, salads) that had never reported an annual profit since its 1998 founding. Persistent margin/demand weakness drove severe cash-flow problems, mass store closures, and a September 2016 Chapter 11 filing followed by an asset sale.
business_type: Fast-casual restaurant chain (company-operated and franchised units)
macro_context: Highly competitive fast-casual segment with rising labor and occupancy costs; chronic unprofitability and thin liquidity at the company.
evidence_summary: Cosi reported approximately $90 million of revenue for fiscal 2015 but had not posted an annual profit since 1998. In 2016, sales declines led to severe cash-flow problems. Immediately before filing, the company closed 29 underperforming company-operated locations; as of October 1, 2016 it operated or franchised 76 restaurants (45 company-operated, 31 franchised). Cosi and subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on September 28, 2016 in the District of Massachusetts and ran a Section 363 asset sale, with LIMAB LLC named winning bidder on November 29, 2016.

source_backed_metrics.chapter_11_venue: U.S. Bankruptcy Court, District of Massachusetts

owner_decision_context: Leadership faced chronic unprofitability and a deteriorating cash position. They had to choose between continued operation on thinning liquidity versus restructuring; they closed underperforming units and ultimately filed Chapter 11 to pursue a going-concern asset sale.
action_taken: Closed 29 underperforming company-operated locations, filed Chapter 11 on 2016-09-28, and pursued a Section 363 sale of substantially all assets, won by LIMAB LLC.
outcome_evidence: Chapter 11 filing on 2016-09-28 with severe cash-flow problems, store count cut to 76, and a 363 asset sale confirm a liquidity-driven bankruptcy rooted in long-run unprofitability.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned HTTP 403; figures confirmed via WebSearch snippets attributed to the Cosi 8-K exhibit and corroborated by named trade press (QSR, Food Business News, Restaurant Dive). Precise net-loss figures and same-store-sales percentages were not cleanly confirmable from primary snippets and are omitted. Cosi later filed bankruptcy again (2020); this record concerns the 2016 filing only.
directly_stated: Cosi filed voluntary Chapter 11 on September 28, 2016 in the District of Massachusetts
The company had not reported an annual profit since its 1998 founding
29 underperforming company-operated locations were closed immediately before filing
As of October 1, 2016 it operated or franchised 76 restaurants (45 company, 31 franchised)
LIMAB LLC was the Section 363 winning bidder, announced November 29, 2016
inferred: Chronic margin/demand weakness (never profitable) was the underlying condition; the acute trigger was a cash/liquidity crisis
Store closures were a reactive cash-preservation move rather than a growth strategy
why_useful_for_opsiq: Mid-market restaurant chain with chronic unprofitability tipping into an acute cash/liquidity crisis and bankruptcy, with both company-operated and franchised units. Tests whether the engine distinguishes the chronic business condition (structural margin/demand failure since inception) from the acute liquidity trigger, and whether it escalates review cadence as liquidity deteriorates.
